title: Ashtpadi 24, salok: the perfect Lord
hookLine: pooraa prabh aaraadhiaa: I worshiped the perfect Lord (Sukhmani 24)

lines: A WORD WORN DOWN TO FINE.
cards: Listen to how often you say perfect in a day. The barista asks if oat milk is okay: perfect. A coworker says the meeting moved to three: perfect.

A friend is running ten minutes late: perfect. We've worn the word down until it means fine, or got it, or sure. Sukhmani's twenty-fourth ashtpadi opens with that same word, pooraa, four times in two short lines.
And it means it, every time.

teach.b: The salok, in paraphrase: I worshiped the perfect Lord, whose Name is perfect. Nanak has found the perfect One; sing the praises of the perfect One. Pooraa means full, complete, whole, lacking nothing.
A pooraa glass is filled to the top. A pooraa job is finished. When Gurbani calls God pooraa, nothing in God is missing or partial, and nothing needs to be added.
Count it as it goes: the perfect Lord, the perfect Name, the perfect One found, the perfect One praised.
Like a bell rung four times. And look at the order. First aaraadhiaa: I worshiped, I remembered with devotion.
Then paaiaa: I found. Then the invitation, gaau: sing.
Worship leads to finding; finding spills over into song. That's the whole of Sukhmani in miniature.

teach.h: THE LAST SALOK GATHERS IT ALL.
teach.b: It's fitting that this is the last salok.

Over twenty-three ashtpadis, Sukhmani has walked through nearly everything a life holds: pride and humility, slander and praise, wealth that stays behind, the wanderer at the door, the stillness before creation, the eye-ointment of wisdom.
Now it gathers all of that into one word.
Not a summary of the argument; a word of praise. After all the teaching, what's left is gratitude, sung. The word we've worn down to fine gets its weight back: full, whole, lacking nothing.
In these two short lines, only one thing is called that, four times running.

how: Sikhs reciting the final ashtpadi of Sukhmani Sahib begin with a salok that names God pooraa, perfect and whole, four times, moving from worship to finding to song.

s: the twenty-fourth salok uses the word pooraa four times
the perfect Lord, Name, One found, and One praised.
the last salok sums up Sukhmani with an argument
pooraa in Gurbani means roughly fine, or okay
it means full, complete, lacking nothing.

games.q: you've walked all twenty-three ashtpadis. the salok moves worship, finding, then what?
o: song: sing the praises of the perfect One.
games.why: gaau: sing. finding the perfect One spills over into praise, which is how Sukhmani's last salok ends.

practice: Let one thing that's full and good come to mind, a person's kindness, a view, a piece of music, the fact of your own breathing, and stay with it until gratitude rises on its own.
Then let it out once, in a single word or phrase, and rest in the quiet after it. If you pray, the word can be Waheguru, itself a word of wonder and praise.

wordCard.voice: Pooraa, full, perfect, complete: its salok rings pooraa four times: the perfect Lord, the perfect Name, the perfect One found, the perfect One praised.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: pooraa, full, perfect, complete; rung four times in the last salok.

carryVoice: Your line: the perfect one. Not fine, not okay, but full and lacking nothing. See you tomorrow.
